solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Two ponies traversing island, running freely

indicators.note: to traverse is to cross from side to side, so the ponies' letters stretch across the island and sit on either side of it

parts.note: a pony is £25 in slang, so two are fifty quid: L (Roman fifty) + QUID

explanation.surface: A pair of ponies splashing across an island, galloping free.
explanation.walkthrough: A pony is British slang for £25, and a quid is a pound, so two ponies are L QUID; I goes in after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: a liquid is matter that runs freely, flowing rather than holding a shape.

clue.text: This may keep you afloat if you live around south of lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is south of a piece is written below it, so it follows that piece

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: around asks for the words you live to be read backwards

parts.note: to live is to be, exist

explanation.surface: A conditional promise of buoyancy to someone living near a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live' is to be, exist; 'south of' works because this is a down clue, where later letters sit lower.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifebuoy is a floating ring thrown to someone in the water to stop them sinking.

clue.text: What for Guatemalan flag's filling empty spot up

definitions.text: What for Guatemalan flag's filling empty spot up

parts.note: Guatemalans speak Spanish, in which 'what' is que

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, i.e. backwards
the filling of a word is its inside, all but the first and last letters

parts.note: the word flag, whose inner letters are wanted

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: a zit is a pimple, a spot

explanation.surface: Something odd is wanted for the middle of Guatemala's national flag.
explanation.walkthrough: Guatemala is Spanish-speaking, hence the Spanish word for what; 'up' works because this is a down clue. As a whole the clue also describes the bird, which sits at the centre of Guatemala's flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The resplendent quetzal, a bright green bird, is the emblem pictured in the centre of the Guatemalan flag; it also names the country's currency.

clue.text: On the spot where scripture's penned by saintly itinerant

indicators.note: something penned by another is shut inside it, as in a pen
an itinerant wanders about, so the letters of saintly are moved around

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a body of scripture

explanation.surface: A wandering holy man writes out scripture wherever he happens to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saintly itinerant' reads as a wandering holy man, but 'itinerant' only tells you to rearrange the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the spot means doing it at once, immediately, without delay.

clue.text: Barge afloat, but with no hint of underdeck?

definitions.text: Barge afloat, but with no hint of underdeck?

indicators.note: to barge is to push and jostle, so these letters are knocked into a new order
a hint of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: the word underdeck, whose first letter is taken away

explanation.surface: A query about a floating barge that has nothing below its deck.
explanation.walkthrough: Take AFLOATBUT, remove U (the hint of underdeck) and rearrange the rest. As a whole the clue describes the vessel: a flat-bottomed barge with no hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatboat is a broad, flat-bottomed river barge for carrying goods, with no deep hull below decks.

clue.text: Sheds and banks of earthen works by abandoned sinister property

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two parts sit side by side

parts.note: something abandoned has been left behind

indicators.note: works suggests the letters are worked over into a new form
the banks of a word are its two edges, its first and last letters

parts.note: the word earthen, whose outside letters are wanted

explanation.surface: Abandoned earthworks with sheds and embankments make a gloomy, sinister estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks of earthen' gives EN; 'works' rearranges SHEDS AND EN into HANDEDNESS. Sinister is Latin for left, which is why the property is unlucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister originally meant on the left side, so the quality of favouring the left hand is a sinister trait.

clue.text: Nancy's very bored by sun making hair curl?

indicators.note: to be bored is to be drilled through

parts.note: French for very; Nancy is a French city

explanation.surface: A bored woman called Nancy curling her hair in the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy looks like a woman's name, but it is the French city, which signals a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonym: a tress is a long lock of hair, often worn in curls, so the question mark hedges.

clue.text: Starting to argue is violation of decency

indicators.note: to start is to jump in alarm, so the letters jolt out of order

explanation.surface: A stuffy view that even beginning an argument is indecent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starting' reads as 'beginning', which sends the solver looking for a first letter; it is the anagram indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an outrage is a gross offence against public decency or morals.

clue.text: Endpoint of serialist composer's journey

indicators.note: the endpoint of a word is where it stops, its last letter

explanation.surface: Where a twelve-tone composer's career ended up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Journey' sounds like a career arc, but it is a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, as noun or verb: a journey is a spell of travel, and to journey is to travel.

clue.text: Uncompromising and on time, stage grips out to lunch after play

parts.note: a raised platform, split around MENTAL

explanation.surface: A strict, punctual stagehand crew going out to lunch after the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage grips' reads as theatre crew; here 'grips' is the verb, DAIS holding MENTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjectival use: a fundamentalist stance holds strictly to basic doctrine and admits no compromise.

clue.text: Putting daughter in charge, pack lunch for the kids?

indicators.note: putting with in says one piece is placed inside the others
with putting, it asks for the letter to go inside

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
to pack a bag is to stuff it

explanation.surface: A parent hands the daughter responsibility for packing the children's school lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The kids are young goats, not children, which is what makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Feedstuff is fodder for livestock, and kids are young goats, so it is food for them.

clue.text: Rat, heartlessly put in sack, turned and bit performer

indicators.note: turned means the combined letters are read back to front
put in means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: to give someone the axe is to sack them

indicators.note: heartlessly removes the middle, leaving the outside letters

parts.note: the word rat, whose first and last letters are kept

explanation.surface: A rat thrown in a bag turns and bites someone performing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' is the verb, to fire someone, not a bag; the reversal applies after the insertion is made.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a film actor with a small non-speaking part, the most minor of performers.

clue.text: Glider advanced beyond ring road

indicators.note: beyond means further along

parts.note: give someone a ring = give them a buzz

explanation.surface: A glider flying past a ring road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glider' suggests an aircraft; it is a soaring bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by behaviour: a buzzard is a hawk that soars and glides on thermals for long stretches.

clue.text: Pawn to be exchanged, only for men to get into scrape

indicators.note: to get into something is to go inside it

parts.note: to hoe is to scrape the soil
a stag night is men only

explanation.surface: A chess pawn traded, and men getting into a scrape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pawn' suggests chess, but a hostage is a human pawn held for exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a pawn is someone used by others, and a hostage is held to be traded for demands.

clue.text: Old damp blankets left for youngster prowling after dark

indicators.note: to blanket is to cover completely

explanation.surface: Damp old blankets left out for a child wandering at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blankets' reads as bedding for the youngster; it is the verb, WET covering L.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: an owlet is a young owl, and owls hunt at night.

clue.text: Divine petite guide losing heart

explanation.surface: Praise for a tiny, heartbroken guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' reads as an adjective; it is the noun, a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: a divine is a cleric or theologian, and a minister is a member of the clergy.

clue.text: One carving up outside of writing implement?

definitions.text: One carving up outside of writing implement?

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it

parts.note: one who carves up, or divides, something; split SHAR...ER

explanation.surface: A violent sort slashing the exterior of a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads straight too: a pencil sharpener carves away the outside of a writing implement.
explanation.definitionFit: &lit: a pencil sharpener shaves the outer wood off a pencil, carving the outside of a writing implement.

clue.text: Set the bell swinging around noon

indicators.note: around means the outer letters surround the next piece
a swinging bell moves back and forth, so its letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Getting the church bell ringing at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a verb about ringing the bell; it is the adjective, as in set on doing something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being set on something means being determined to do it, just as being hellbent on it does.

clue.text: Ace singer-songwriter dropping round for a break

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: dropping says the round letter leaves the singer's name
for says the letter a goes in where the round letter was

explanation.surface: A top singer-songwriter skips a round in order to take a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping round for a' reads as one instruction: the round letter goes and a takes its place. Beyoncé is an American pop star.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter in abeyance is suspended for a time, so abeyance is a pause or break.

clue.text: Leader to bring fraud group together

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so the leader to bring is its first letter

explanation.surface: A ringleader assembling a gang for a scam.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a gang boss; 'Leader to bring' just takes the B.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to bracket items is to class them together, as brackets enclose a group.

clue.text: Person who settled down here to fish

definitions.meaning: a member of the Germanic tribe that settled 'here', in England, and gave it its name
to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: A settler who put down roots here to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angles were a Germanic people who settled in England, which is named after them; 'here' is Britain, where The Times is printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an Angle was one of the tribes that settled England, and to angle is to fish with rod and line.

clue.text: Lower gear for cycling club

indicators.note: cycling goes round and round

parts.note: gear or kit; cycled to GRI

explanation.surface: Advice to shift into a low gear at the cycling club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is not about gears: it is the verb lower (rhymes with 'flower'), to scowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncommon verb: to lower, or lour, is to frown or scowl, which is to grimace.

clue.text: Vacuous idiot claiming he's joking, turning off and on printer

indicators.note: claiming means taking hold of, so the outer letters enclose the rest
vacuous means empty, so only the outside letters stay

parts.note: the word idiot, whose outside letters are kept

indicators.note: turning means those picked letters are read backwards
off and on means every other letter is taken, skipping the first

parts.note: the words he's joking, from which alternate letters are picked

explanation.surface: A dim-witted person says they're joking while switching the printer off and on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off and on' picks EJKN from HESJOKING (the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters); 'turning' gives NKJE, which 'Vacuous idiot' (IT) claims.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkjet is a kind of computer printer that sprays tiny droplets of ink onto paper.

clue.text: Horse gets to Fence 1 … horse almost falls

indicators.note: to fence something is to enclose it
'almost' cuts a letter off

explanation.surface: A racecourse commentary: a horse reaches the first fence, and another nearly falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' reads as the horse coming down; it is the definition, as in Niagara Falls.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper-name definition: Niagara is the famous set of falls on the US–Canada border.

clue.text: American river flowing out of range of hearing

parts.note: the Ural river rises in the Ural mountains

explanation.surface: An American river running beyond earshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range of hearing' looks like the phrase; the break comes after 'range', and the Ural is both a river and a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: aural comes from Latin auris, ear, and means relating to hearing.

clue.text: Joke about having run away from ordeal of marriage

indicators.note: about here means turned around, read backwards

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

indicators.note: having with away from says one letter has gone from the next word
with having, it asks for run's letter to be taken out

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A wry remark that someone has fled the ordeal of married life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordeal of marriage' reads as one phrase, but the ordeal is wordplay and 'of marriage' is the adjectival definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptial is an adjective meaning relating to a wedding or to married life.

clue.text: US player discarding clubs on turning over card

indicators.note: discarding means the clubs letter is thrown out of the athlete word

parts.note: jock is American slang for an athlete or sports player
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: turning over means the word for on is read backwards

explanation.surface: An American player throws away a club and flips over a card.
explanation.walkthrough: JOCK without C is JOK; RE, meaning on, reverses to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The joker is an extra playing card in a standard pack, often wild.

clue.text: Intimate admonition to first couple overheard?

indicators.note: overheard means caught by ear, so the words count by their sound

parts.note: what might be said to Adam and Eve after the apple

explanation.surface: A private scolding of Adam and Eve, eavesdropped on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate' looks like an adjective about the scolding; it is the verb, to hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to intimate (stress on the last syllable) is to hint indirectly, which is what insinuating does.

clue.text: All women objectified strapping boxer

indicators.note: to strap is to bind round

parts.note: British slang for attractive women seen as objects; split TOT...TY

explanation.surface: Every woman leering at a well-built boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strapping' reads as brawny, describing the boxer; it is the container verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun synonym: 'the all' and the totality both mean the whole of something, every part included.

clue.text: Someone bothering about the teaching of religion?

definitions.text: Someone bothering about the teaching of religion?

parts.note: Religious Instruction, the old British school subject

explanation.surface: A tiresome person who goes on about religious teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a priest concerns himself with teaching religion.
explanation.definitionFit: &lit, with a wry question mark: a priest is professionally bothered about teaching the faith.
